en.title: Robot Movement Reachability
en.description:
A robot starts at positive integer coordinates (x1,y1) and can perform (x,y)→(x+y,y) or (x,y)→(x,x+y) any number of times. Determine whether it can reach (x2,y2).

The ranges of the start and end points and the two moves are precisely defined; this site specifies stdin/stdout.

Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/weride#5-bot-movement-reachability-two-move-types (fixed statement fingerprint b1639717ffbe4708cefb3029bfffbbb3d069343624539d09b7792a5e067eb34c). The input/output protocol and bounds added by this site are as described in the statement and are not claimed to be rules of the original site.
en.input: One line with four integers x1 y1 x2 y2 (each in 1..1000).
en.output: Output Yes if reachable, otherwise output No.
en.explanation: See the accompanying notes for the full approach, proof, and complexity.
hints: Walk backward from the target: if x>y, the last step can only come from (x−y,y); otherwise it comes from (x,y−x). Once a coordinate drops below the start, it is impossible.
